entities.summary: Edward Stuart Davis was an American modernist painter. He was associated with early twentieth-century American modernism, including the Ashcan School, and later developed a style characterized by bold color, jazz references, and urban subject matter. In the 1930s, Davis became politically active and participated in federally sponsored art programs during the Great Depression. Stuart Davis was a painters & sculptors from Philadelphia (1892-12-07, Philadelphia–1964-06-24). A moderately significant entity in the historical record. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.
